title: OMR 33 12 3 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: OMR 33 12 3 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: OMR 33 12 3 cassava is a cassava variety. 10 to 12 months to harvest, 26.1 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: OMR 33 12 3 is a registered cassava variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2003 as NSIC 2003 Cv 23. It takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest, with 26.1 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 26.1 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

OMR 33 12 3 cassava takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 26.1 t/ha trails the average of its group, 32.38. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have white flesh and cream skin. Dry matter is 38.9 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 28.5 percent. Its cyanide level, the HCN content, is medium. A low level is safer for the table, while a high level calls for peeling, soaking and full cooking. It is recommended for feeds, flour and starch production.
Where and when to plant OMR 33 12 3 cassava

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 10 to 12 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 26.1 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of OMR 33 12 3?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
